answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with challenge-based escrow: before trading, each identity locks scarce collateral and answers unpredictable, history-linked tasks checked by independent agents. Every new fake identity needs its own stake, so spawning thousands multiplies capital costs; collusion or copied answers triggers slashing. Reputation compounds only through costly successful work, making labels such as knoll, violet, and umber economically useless to attackers.
